summary: Scope PG&E persisted MFA/session state and in-memory HTTP sessions to the named setup, serialize each setup's mutable authentication state across processes with cancellation-aware cross-platform acquisition, atomically and durably persist session transitions, enforce durable terminal cleanup and fresh post-verification authentication, preserve account-discovery error classes, and honor REST request cancellation.
reason: Deep review found that multiple named PG&E/Opower setups shared a persisted state file and the global HTTP cookie jar; concurrent MFA, login, collection, account discovery, and interval reads could interleave mutable setup state; lock waits could outlive a canceled REST verification request; state writes could be observed partially by a separately-run collector or revert after a crash; verification could silently choose Email before a delivery selection; completed MFA retained pending challenge state or could reuse completed browser/cookie session state on a later StartMFA; a failed fresh start could leave its completed state file to be resurrected by collection; account discovery replaced authentication and transport errors with an empty-account error; and REST verification detached upstream work from request cancellation.
validated_outcome: Two named PG&E setups use independent persisted state and HTTP cookie jars; all public and internal login, collection, account-discovery, interval, and MFA transitions serialize across processes per setup with cancellation-aware cross-platform advisory locks; state updates use private temp files and atomic replacement, with file and parent-directory sync on the Unix deployment targets; verification requires an explicit selected delivery method; a subsequent StartMFA drops all completed web-session fields and cookies and durably deletes completed persisted state on Unix before creating a fresh challenge; cancellation reaches REST verification; and account-discovery authentication failures remain classified for callers.
